purpose: Discharge steps 2 and 3 of directives/e256-hardware-architecture.md §5: bound the H5 schedule cost per block, and re-certify the H3 offset rotor and H4 keyed wiring against the same structural obligations the E256-062 receipt already discharged for the programmable-affine construction.

exploratory_probe_disclosure.statement: An exploratory probe was run before this preregistration was frozen. It confirmed the XOR-offset spectral invariance, that the additive-offset alternative breaks the spectrum, that repeated offsets never reach all-to-all diffusion, and the arithmetic form of the schedule accounting.
exploratory_probe_disclosure.consequence: Predictions below are therefore stated qualitatively and structurally. Every exact count — the size of the certified wiring set, the compression and permutation totals, and the cost ratio — is reported as a measured output and is deliberately NOT preregistered as a number.
exploratory_probe_disclosure.reason: Freezing counts already observed in a probe would be post-hoc dressing rather than prediction.

questions.text: Does the H3 offset rotor preserve the exact AES differential, linear, and algebraic spectrum across the complete offset space rather than a sample?
Which row-offset tuples may enter the H4 keyed wiring set, and is pairwise distinctness sufficient to qualify?
Does every member of the certified wiring set inherit the E256-062 structural obligations, including the four-round active-rotor bound?
How many primitive invocations per 32-byte block does an XOF schedule need against the per-derivation HMAC-SHA512 model?

toolchain_contract.deterministic_operations: integer and byte operations only; no floating-point value enters the deterministic payload except explicitly labelled rounded ratios

h3_rotor.formula: R(x) = SBOX(x XOR p_in) XOR p_out
h3_rotor.spectrum_scope: exhaustive over all 256 values of p_in; p_out contributes only an output translation, which cannot change differential magnitudes, linear magnitudes, or algebraic degree
h3_rotor.spectrum_argument: For any a, R(x) XOR R(x XOR a) = SBOX(y) XOR SBOX(y XOR a) under y = x XOR p_in, and y ranges over all 256 values, so the differential distribution is identical to the S-box for every offset pair. Linear magnitudes are preserved because p_out only flips a sign and p_in only permutes the input, and degree is preserved because composition with an affine bijection and XOR of a constant preserve algebraic degree.
h3_rotor.metric_definitions: identical to directives/e256-wide-preregistration.json: DDT maximum over input difference 1..255; LAT maximum absolute value over input and output masks 1..255; algebraic degree as maximum coordinate ANF degree computed separately for the forward and inverse maps

h4_wiring.candidate_space: all ordered 4-tuples of pairwise distinct row offsets drawn from 0..7
certification_obligations: row shift is a byte permutation with an exact inverse
all 69 nonempty square MixColumns minors nonzero over GF(2^8)
MixColumns branch number 5 with an exact two-sided inverse
structural all-to-all byte dependency reached by round 3
four-round active-rotor lower bound of 25 under the inherited wide-trail obligation manifest
h4_wiring.certified_set_definition: the subset of the candidate space for which every certification obligation holds; its size is a measured output, not a preregistered number
h4_wiring.keyed_selection_note: A keyed wiring selection may only draw from the certified set. Selecting from the full distinct-offset space is forbidden unless the certified set is proven to equal it.

h5_schedule.material_composition: 384 rotor-selection bytes for 12 rounds by 32 lanes, followed by 416 mask bytes for mask indices 0 through 12
h5_schedule.canonical_context_bytes: computed from the frozen E256-W canonical context encoding, not asserted

baseline_model.description: the E256-062 model schedule, which issues one HMAC-SHA512 purpose stream per selection byte and per mask index
baseline_model.sha512_compression_accounting: compressions(message_length) = 1 + ceil((message_length + 17) / 128), covering the 0x80 padding byte and the 16-byte length field
baseline_model.hmac_compression_accounting: compressions(inner message) + 2, for the single-block ipad prefix and the two-block outer hash over a 64-byte digest

candidate_model.description: one domain-separated SHAKE-256 squeeze covering the complete material block
candidate_model.permutation_accounting: keccak_f1600_calls = ceil((absorbed_length + 1) / 136) + ceil(output_length / 136) - 1, under the stated convention that the final absorb permutation also produces the first squeeze block
candidate_model.verification: the squeeze must be checked to actually return the full material block length from hashlib.shake_256

h5_schedule.graded_quantity: primitive invocations per 32-byte block for each model, and the ratio between them
h5_schedule.explicit_limitation: This is exact arithmetic accounting plus an output-length check, not an instrumented count inside a hash implementation and not a synthesis or throughput measurement. Selecting a production XOF remains OPEN.

controls.mutation: replace XOR conjugation with additive conjugation modulo 256: R(x) = (SBOX((x + p) mod 256) - p) mod 256
controls.detector: at least one offset yields a differential uniformity or algebraic degree differing from the S-box
controls.rationale: this is the rejected alternative in the architecture record; if the invariance check cannot separate it from XOR conjugation the check has no power

controls.mutation: inject the offset tuple (0,0,0,0) through the normal dependency and dispersion routine
controls.detector: structural all-to-all dependency is not reached within 12 rounds

controls.mutation: inject the offset tuple (0,1,1,3) through the normal dispersion routine
replace MixColumns row 3 with row 2 before structural validation
controls.adapter_exception: expected typed structural rejection occurs before inverse computation because no inverse exists
controls.detector: zero determinant or minor and inverse unavailable

controls.mutation: request fewer than the frozen 800 material bytes from the candidate schedule
controls.detector: material coverage check rejects the short block

control_execution_contract.requirement: Each control must execute exactly its declared shared_path; only a declared adapter_exception may terminate early.
candidate_nulls: the H3 offset rotor must match the S-box spectrum for every one of the 256 p_in values and be bijective for all 65536 offset pairs
the frozen Rijndael tuple (0,1,3,4) must appear in the certified wiring set
the certified wiring set must be non-empty and every member must discharge every obligation
control_execution_contract.fail_closed: Build an in-memory invalid diagnostic, exit nonzero, and refuse to write or accept the canonical receipt on any contract, control, null, or coverage failure.

interpretation.scope: structural certification and arithmetic schedule accounting only
interpretation.next: Re-certification licenses the H8 hardware attack lane against the H3/H4 candidate. It does not license a round count, a production XOF, a byte-exact specification, or production RTL.
interpretation.baseline_result: The fixed-AES comparator retains the same structural bounds, so no rotor-namespace security advantage is established here either.

non_claims: Passing this gate is not IND-CPA, IND-CCA, AEAD, PRP, PRF, or standalone-cipher security.

The four-round bound covers single differential and linear trails only; clustering, integral, algebraic, meet-in-the-middle, rebound, slide, invariant-subspace, related-key, multi-user, and implementation attacks are untested.
Structural byte dependency does not prove the absence of algebraic cancellation.
Exhaustive spectral invariance over the offset space is a statement about one 8-bit rotor, not about the 256-bit permutation.
The schedule figures are arithmetic invocation counts, not throughput, latency, area, or energy measurements, and no production XOF is selected.
A certified wiring set is not a keyed-wiring security argument; how offsets are selected and what that leaks remains OPEN.
No C/H/N row, E256 finding, suite, profile, fixture, or release gate closes here, and reviewed standard AEAD remains mandatory for real data.
